title: SECURITY AWARE POSITION, VELOCITY AND TIME INTEGRITY CONCEPT - EXPRO+
description: ObjectivesTo develop an integrity concept leveraging Position, Velocity and Time (PVT) assurance solutions for safety critical applications.DescriptionSafety critical applications rely on integrity concepts based on protection levels and alerting schemes to bound the position error in nominal and failure scenarios under a given integrity risk. This allows estimating the worst-case user position systematically taking into account potential feared events. Similar integrity concepts and list of feared events can be developed considering the potential presence of intentional GNSS signal impairments.The Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) providers are implementing mechanism in order to protect the users from security threats such as spoofing. For instance, Galileo will provide both navigation message authentication (NMA) and ranging authentication (Commercial Service Authentication [CAS]). Therefore, the user integrity concepts will have to be expanded to define the impact of intentional interference, to specify the related feared events, and to consider the barriers provided by PVT assurance solutions.This activity aims at exploring technological enablers, algorithms and concepts for future positioning integrity concepts, which would enable safe and secure operations even in the presence of potential intentional impairments. It will investigate the contribution to the overall safety and trustworthiness provided by GNSS-based PVT assurance. Moreover, attention will be given to demonstrating that the overall target integrity can be achieved by different positioning solutions and PVT assurance techniques.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- State-of-the-art survey of integrity concepts for PVT, of PVT assurance services, and of anti-spoofing techniques,- Development of innovative security-aware concepts,- Performance assessment of the integrity concepts,- Roadmap for standardization.DeliverablesReport, Software

title: NAVISP-EL1-110-USER EQUIPMENT PLATFORM FOR POSITIONING WITH 5G/6G NON-TERRESTRIAL NETWORKS - EXPRO PLUS
description: The future 5G and 6G non-terrestrial networks (NTN) will offer continuous and ubiquitous coverage, serving predominantly terrestrial users in remote and underserved areas. The latest 3GPP releases imply that the user equipment (UE) must be equipped with the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receiver determining its position, velocity, and time (PVT) to be able to connect to NTN. To alleviate the dependence of UE on GNSS, the use of 5G NTN signals for positioning is being actively studied. Although various conceptsand solutions to provide PVT with NTN have been identified, the development and prototyping of representative user side solutions remain to be addressed in detail. Current NTN system studies would greatly benefit from design, evaluation, and breadboarding of realistic user equipment algorithms and solutions. The activity will design and develop a generic user equipment platform in the form ofhardware and software to evaluate and trade off user-side processing solutions and algorithms for PVT with NTN. The positioning performance of the UE will be validated using a representative NTN simulator.

title: N2O SATELLITE OBSERVATION REQUIREMENTS - EXPRO PLUS
description: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is an important greenhouse gas that also contributes to stratospheric ozone depletion. This study aims at characterising the needs for space-based observations of atmospheric N2O, starting from a user and science perspective. Knowledge gaps are identified related to the N2O production and life cycle, its impact on stratospheric ozone, and its role in the Earth's radiation balance that can be addressed with the help of satellite observations, with a focus on information that can be provided from satellite observations. The study explores the space of requirements that satellite observations of atmospheric N2O (Level-2) and measurements of radiances at the top of the atmosphere (Level-1) would have to meet in order to contribute to addressing these knowledge gaps.
